title: The Murderous Carpool
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0921.txt (355 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Detective-cast (Kogoro, Ran, Conan) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges between the entities involved. case_type: murder (staged to look like an accidental fall/strangulation). Old low-fidelity `cases/ep921_the_murderous_carpool.json` correctly identified the culprit (Komada) and his core motive (Goto stole his thesis), so no culprit-identity correction was needed -- but its mechanism was wrong/oversimplified: it described a plain 'strangles with own phone strap while sleeping' murder and a single generic 'phone strap' object. The transcript shows a more elaborate trick: Komada rigged a dry-ice-packed air cushion under Goto's seat (dry ice sublimating expands ~800x, eventually tipping Goto out of his seat) with Komada's own phone-and-strap threaded through the seat gap toward Goto's neck so the fall itself caused the strangulation; Komada then swapped phones with Goto beforehand so he could call Saeki using Goto's phone to fake that Goto was alive and functioning during the shopping trip (a false alibi window), and later engineered a reason to be first back at the car (carrying groceries) to swap the phones back before the body was found. He was caught because his own old phone had impact damage matching plastic fragments stuck to the blanket, while Goto's recovered phone was undamaged. The old file's 'a year earlier' backstory timing for the thesis theft is not stated that precisely in the transcript, so that detail was dropped rather than asserted. Saeki's and Haruka's motives (career blocked; general resentment) are red herrings raised and dismissed in the interrogation.

clues.desc: The air cushion under Goto was supposedly brand-new yet already had a hole, and was damp though nowhere else on the seat was wet -- points to a hidden trick rather than a defective product.
Plastic fragments stuck to the blanket match dents on Komada's phone, but Goto's own recovered phone shows no such damage -- proves a different phone did the strangling and was later swapped out.
